data.name: Help_Intro
data.value: How to book a spot, what earns you points, and what to do when something goes wrong. Click a question to expand the answer.

data.name: Help_Reserve_Q
data.value: How do I book a parking spot?

data.name: Help_Reserve_A1
data.value: Under Reserve a spot, pick the date and the from–to time and click Find spots. You'll see the free spots and the price in credits for that window. Click Reserve on the spot you want.

data.name: Help_Reserve_A2_Paid
data.value: When you arrive, confirm it with Check in; when you leave, click Complete. If you end up not needing the spot, release it — do it at least {0} before the start and you get the full credits back plus points for making it available to others.

data.name: Help_Reserve_A2_Free
data.value: When you arrive, confirm it with Check in; when you leave, click Complete. If you end up not needing the spot, release it as early as you can so somebody else can use it.

data.name: Help_Credits_Q
data.value: What are credits and why does the price change?

data.name: Help_Credits_A1
data.value: Bookings are paid with credits from your wallet. The base price is {0}; during peak hours ({1}–{2}) and when the lot fills up it rises, up to {3}. Scarce slots cost more, which keeps the cheaper times available for those who can arrive at another hour.

data.name: Help_Credits_Li1
data.value: Once a month you automatically receive {0}.

data.name: Help_Credits_Li1_Tiered
data.value: Once a month you automatically receive {0}, plus {1} more for every tier you have reached.

data.name: Help_Credits_Li2
data.value: Cancelling or releasing at least {0} before the start refunds the full amount you paid.

data.name: Help_Credits_Li3
data.value: Not showing up without releasing means the credits you paid are forfeited.

data.name: Help_Points_Q
data.value: What earns points and what are they for?

data.name: Help_Points_A1
data.value: Points are a reputation score for the leaderboard — spending credits never lowers them. You earn them for behaviour that helps everyone else:

data.name: Help_Points_Li1
data.value: Completing a booking (actually using the spot): each one in an unbroken streak adds {0}, up to {1}. Paid once a day.

data.name: Help_Points_Li2
data.value: Parking outside the peak window: {0} extra (peak is {1}–{2}).

data.name: Help_Points_Li3
data.value: Releasing a booking you don't need: from {0} points up to {1} depending on how badly the spot is wanted; at most {2}× a day.

data.name: Help_Points_Li4
data.value: Sharing your own resident spot, or taking a shared one (scaled by your verified commute).

data.name: Help_Points_A2
data.value: Points determine your tier: Bronze, Silver from {0}, Gold from {1} and Platinum from {2}. A higher tier brings:

data.name: Help_Points_Perk_Queue
data.value: queue priority (a long-waiting lower tier still catches up),

data.name: Help_Points_Perk_Allowance
data.value: a bigger monthly credit allowance (+{0} per tier),

data.name: Help_Points_Perk_Discount
data.value: a discount on bookings ({0} % per tier).

data.name: Help_Points_Decay
data.value: Points drop by {0} % every {1}, so they are kept up by staying active — and old penalties heal the same way.

data.name: Help_NoShow_Q
data.value: What happens if I don't turn up?

data.name: Help_NoShow_A1
data.value: If you neither use nor release the booking, the system marks it as a no-show {0} after the start and the credits you paid are forfeited. You get a reminder shortly before the start so it doesn't slip your mind.

data.name: Help_NoShow_A1_Penalty
data.value: If you neither use nor release the booking, the system marks it as a no-show {0} after the start: the credits you paid are forfeited, {1} are deducted and your completion streak resets. You get a reminder shortly before the start so it doesn't slip your mind.

data.name: Help_NoShow_A2
data.value: None of that happens if you release the spot in time — instead you get your credits back and earn points. Releasing is worth it even at the last minute.

data.name: Help_Queue_Q
data.value: What if my slot is fully booked?

data.name: Help_Queue_A1
data.value: Join the queue — it's free. As soon as a spot frees up for your window, the system holds it for you for {0} minutes and sends a notification and an email with a Claim the spot button. Until then nobody else can book it.

data.name: Help_Queue_A2
data.value: The queue is served by waiting time. If you miss the claim window, the spot goes to the next in line and you rejoin at the back.

data.name: Help_Queue_A2_Tiered
data.value: The order blends your tier with how long you've waited, so a lower tier still gets served. If you miss the claim window, the spot goes to the next in line and you rejoin at the back.

data.name: Help_Queue_Penalty
data.value: Note: a no-show on a spot claimed from the queue is penalised more heavily — {0}, {1} and {2} without access to the queue.

data.name: Help_Blocked_Q
data.value: Someone else's car is on my spot. Now what?

data.name: Help_Blocked_A1
data.value: Click "I can't park" on your booking and attach a photo of the blocked spot (mandatory — we use it to verify the situation, and each photo can be used only once). We'll either find you another free spot for the same window (the payment carries over, you pay nothing extra) or cancel the booking with a full refund. Either way it never counts as a no-show.

data.name: Help_Blocked_A2
data.value: As an apology you're due a voucher for one free booking — peak included. We first verify the report from your photo; once the check is done the voucher activates, stays valid for 30 days and is redeemed by ticking the box when booking. It helps if you copy the blocking car's plate into the form: the admin can then tell whether it's a colleague or a vehicle from outside the system.

data.name: Help_Resident_A1
data.value: Your spot is held for you every day until {0}. If you're coming that day, confirm it with Confirm arrival. If you neither confirm nor release it, the spot is offered to everyone else after that hour.

data.name: Help_Resident_A2_Rewarded
data.value: When you know in advance you won't need it, release it (even for several days at once) — you earn {0} for every hour of notice, up to {1} a day. The reward applies up to a monthly limit you set yourself.

data.name: Help_Resident_A2
data.value: When you know in advance you won't need it, release it (even for several days at once) so somebody else can use it.

data.name: Help_Notifications_A1
data.value: Alerts arrive in the bell in the header. You can install the app on your phone or desktop and enable push notifications — then a queue offer or a reminder reaches you even with the app closed. We only email what matters: deadline-driven queue offers, penalties and account security changes.

data.name: Help_Notifications_A2
data.value: Every booking has an Add to calendar button — it downloads an event for Outlook, Google and Apple Calendar, including a reminder 30 minutes ahead. In your profile you can mute notifications temporarily or turn off the free-capacity tips.

data.name: Help_Profile_Q
data.value: What to set up in your profile

data.name: Help_Profile_A1
data.value: Your profile shapes what the app offers you and what you earn points for:

data.name: Help_Profile_Li1
data.value: Home address — once verified, it increases the reward for taking a shared spot based on your commute.

data.name: Help_Profile_Li2
data.value: License plate (saved under My account) — lets the admin find you if your car ever blocks someone's booking, so you hear about it first.

data.name: Help_Profile_Li3
data.value: Team or department — puts you on the team leaderboard.

data.name: Help_Visitors_Q
data.value: How to book a spot for a visitor

data.name: Help_Visitors_A1
data.value: Under Visitors, pick the window and a free visitor spot, then fill in the guest's name (company and plate are recommended). The guest needs no account and no credits.

data.name: Help_Visitors_A2
data.value: If you pick a host, they get a notification telling them where their guest parks. Visitor spots are carved out of the regular pool, so employees cannot take them — they are managed only here.

data.name: Help_Visitors_NoSpots
data.value: There is no active "Visitor" spot yet — until you create one under Parking spots, the visitor agenda has nothing to offer.

data.name: Help_Mismatch_Q
data.value: Occupancy mismatches — who blocked the spot

data.name: Help_Mismatch_A1
data.value: When a driver reports that they couldn't park at their reserved spot, the record shows up under Occupancy mismatches. Each row lists the bookings that met the window on that spot — typically whoever booked it and never arrived — and you can email them in one click.

data.name: Help_Mismatch_A2
data.value: If the driver noted the plate, the system matches it against registered employee vehicles and visitor bookings. "Not in the system" means a vehicle nobody has registered — grounds for security or the lot rules. Repeated mismatches on one spot point to a lasting problem.

data.name: Help_Rules_A1
data.value: Rules and pricing tunes the whole economy at runtime: base price and surcharges, points and penalties, tiers and their perks, the queue, resident rules and the anti-abuse limits. Changes take effect immediately, with no redeployment.

data.name: Help_Rules_State_Pricing
data.value: Adaptive pricing (a controller tunes the peak surcharge toward a target occupancy): {0}.

data.name: Help_Rules_CampaignSetup
data.value: The tip goes out once the lookahead of {2} contains a consecutive stretch of at least {0} below {1} % occupancy. It is sent at most once a day at {3}:00 (workdays only), to the bell and push only — never email — and users can switch it off in their profile.

Residents who release the spot themselves earn points — the earlier the release and the higher the monthly share allowance on the spot, the more.

data.name: Profile_CommuteHelp
data.value: Enter your home address – we compute the distance to the lot from it. The farther you live, the more points you earn for taking a freed spot.

data.name: Parking_Settings_DistanceHelp
data.value: The lot coordinates are used to compute users' commute distance. The reward for taking a shared spot is multiplied by the commute over the reference distance (capped by the multiplier limit) — long-distance commuters earn more. Without a known distance no reward is granted.

data.name: Parking_Settings_TakenBase

data.name: Profile_CommutePrivacy

data.name: Parking_Settings_LimitsHelp
data.value: Abuse safeguards: home addresses within the limit are verified automatically (farther ones go to the admin), and caps bound how many releases per day are rewarded and how long a range can be released at once.

data.name: Parking_Error_InsufficientCredit
data.value: You don't have enough credits for this reservation.

data.name: Parking_Settings_EconomyHelp
data.value: Reservation price in credits: base × peak surcharge × occupancy surcharge, never below the base and never above the cap. Credits are charged when booking; cancelling or releasing early refunds them in full.

data.name: Parking_Settings_QueuePenaltyHelp
data.value: Claiming a freed spot from the waitlist and not arriving blocks everyone behind. The penalty is therefore harsher than a normal no-show: a bigger point deduction, a credit fine, a temporary waitlist ban and a cut to the next monthly allowance.

data.name: Parking_Queue_Error_Banned
data.value: You're temporarily barred from the queue because of a previous no-show.

data.name: Parking_Settings_DemandRewardHelp
data.value: The more wanted the freed spot, the more points: the base reward gains an occupancy surcharge plus a bonus per person waiting in the queue, up to the cap. Freeing a spot when demand peaks pays the most.

data.name: Parking_Settings_LoyaltyHelp
data.value: Reputation tier thresholds Bronze → Silver → Gold → Platinum. The tier follows the current points and unlocks the perks configured below.

data.name: Parking_Settings_AdaptiveHelp
data.value: At the given interval the controller measures peak occupancy and nudges the peak price toward the target occupancy — in bounded steps and only within the limits. Deviations inside the deadband are left alone. When disabled, the manually set peak price applies.

data.name: Parking_Settings_TrustHelp
data.value: Completed reservations on shared spots build an interaction graph; a weighted PageRank turns it into a 0–100 trust score. Reaching the threshold awards the “Trusted” badge. Edges only come from genuinely completed reservations, so the score cannot be farmed for free.

data.name: Parking_Settings_CollusionHelp
data.value: Looks for pairs whose spot sharing concentrates suspiciously on each other — the typical pattern of coordinated point farming. A finding is stored for manual review; automatically only the pair's weight in the trust graph is capped, sanctions stay with the admin.

data.name: Fleet_Admin_Intro
data.value: The registry of company vehicles by license plate. When a user saves a plate to their account and the vehicle's driver email matches their account, they can pair with the vehicle using an emailed confirmation code — and become the resident of its assigned spot.

data.name: Fleet_Admin_EmailHint
data.value: Self-service pairing requires all three: a matching plate saved in the account, a driver email equal to the account's email, and an emailed confirmation code. A vehicle without a driver email (pool car) can only be paired manually here.
